correctness.rationale: After exact reduction to three cube-root samples, normalization gives squared samples \(1+r\cos(\phi+2\pi j/3)\). Convexity in \(r\) forces \(r=1\), hence equal coefficient moduli. At \(r=1\) the elementary symmetric functions are \(e_1=3\), \(e_2=9/4\), and \(e_3=q=(1+\cos(3\phi))/4\). For interior \(q\), differentiating the three roots of \(t^3-3t^2+(9/4)t-q\) shows that the derivative of the \(s\)-th power sum is \(s\) times the second divided difference of \(t^{s-1}\); its sign is the sign of \((s-1)(s-2)\). The endpoint root triples are \((0,3/2,3/2)\) and \((2,1/2,1/2)\), which give the formulas and complete equality cases. The finite verifier only corroborates these identities and does not replace the proof.

value.rationale: The sharp \(\Lambda(p)\) constant is a standard harmonic-analysis invariant, and order three is the first torsion pair where non-even moments have a nontrivial relative-phase choice. The theorem gives the complete real-\(p\) answer and exposes an exact qualitative reversal at \(p=4\): anti-alignment below four, complete phase degeneracy at four, and alignment above four. That structural transition is mathematically motivated and is not a routine interpolation of the known even moments.
